paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage teaches me. God had promised Abram offspring, and Sarai still had no children, so she came up with her own plan (Genesis 15:5; 16:1-2). Abram listened to the voice of Sarai, and the whole house got tangled up: Hagar despised her mistress, Sarai blamed Abram, and Hagar fled (Genesis 16:2-6). I've rushed a batch because I was tired of waiting, and you get a cookie that looks done and tastes like regret.

But look where the angel of the LORD finds Hagar: by a spring in the desert, and he calls her by name (Genesis 16:7-8). Then he tells her, "the LORD has heard your cry of affliction" (Genesis 16:11). She names Him "the God who sees me," and I'm telling you, I know that feeling from the back of a drawer (Genesis 16:13).

So here's your big idea, baker. When waiting gets long, we reach for shortcuts, and shortcuts can leave people hurting. But God doesn't lose track of anybody, and He heard Hagar out there in the desert. If you feel unseen today, remember Hagar at that spring. And keep the oven warm, because this story is not over.
